abstract.text: Reporting bugs is a great way for anyone to help improve Swift. The open source Swift project uses GitHub Issues for tracking bugs.

When opening an issue, please include the following:
A concise description of the problem.
If the issue is a crash, include a stack trace. Otherwise, describe the behavior you were expecting to see, along with the behavior you actually observed.

Double-check that your test case reproduces the issue. A relatively small sample (roughly within 50 lines of code) is best pasted directly into the description; a larger one may be uploaded as an attachment. Consider reducing the sample to the smallest amount of code possible—a smaller test case is easier to reason about and more appealing to сontributors.
A description of the environment that reproduces the problem.
Include information about the Swift compiler’s version, the deployment target (if explicitly set) and your platform.

abstract.text: Understand the process the Swift project uses to evolve the language.

This contributor ladder defines the roles you might gain while contributing to Swift on GitHub. Each role has privileges associated, which requires building trust with the community of contributors. We recognize there are many different types of contributors to Swift and we appreciate every single one! Everyone who has participated in the open source Swift project is a
: This can be by writing code, answering questions on the forums, reporting or triaging bugs, or participating in the Swift evolution process.
Understand identifying introductory issues that are good starting points for developers new to contributing to Swift.
Learn about the community channels for the Swift project.

The Swift.org community has the singular goal of making the world’s best general purpose programming language. Collectively we will develop the language in the open, with contributions from anyone who wishes to participate. This guideline document describes how the Swift community is organized so that we can work together to add amazing new capabilities to Swift, and make it available to even more developers across more platforms.
Reporting bugs is an important part of improving software.
Nearly as important is triaging those bugs to ensure that they are reproducible, small, and unique.
This repository houses processes, policies, and procedures that relate to the operation of the Swift project.
